title: Percentage Yield and Limiting Reagent Calculation

references.label: NCERT Chemistry Part I, Class 11 — Some Basic Concepts of Chemistry

explanation: Theoretical yield is the maximum possible product calculated purely from stoichiometry, based on the LIMITING reagent (never the excess reagent). Actual yield is what is genuinely obtained in a real experiment, always less than or equal to the theoretical yield due to side reactions, incomplete reactions, or handling losses. Percentage yield is a practical efficiency measure and should never legitimately exceed 100%.

variables.meaning: Maximum possible product mass/moles calculated from the limiting reagent

workedExample.scenario: A reaction's theoretical yield is 50 g of product; the experiment actually produces 42 g.

commonMistakes: Calculating theoretical yield using the EXCESS reagent instead of the LIMITING reagent — this always overstates the true maximum possible product.
Reporting a percentage yield above 100% as a genuine result — this signals an experimental/measurement error (e.g. impure or wet product), never a real 'better than theoretical' outcome.
genZNote: Percentage yield: the honest report card on how close your real reaction got to its theoretical best.
